questions.question: What is progressive disclosure for a repository?
options: Load every file in the repository immediately
Hide all documentation from the agent entirely
Replace every test file with a short summary
Show a map and open detail when relevant
questions.explanation: A map-first read set controls context while preserving access to detail.

questions.question: Why skip generated directories in an index?
options: They add noise and are rarely source truth
They are always marked secret and unreadable
They cannot contain readable text at all
They make the Python interpreter run slower
questions.explanation: Generated output competes with relevant source files.

questions.question: What should a root router do?
options: Contain the entire codebase inline
Run production deploys on a schedule
Point to state, rules, and verification
Replace the task contract for every session
questions.explanation: The router directs the agent to deeper sources of truth.

questions.question: What makes an index useful to a task?
options: Alphabetical order only, regardless of the task
Deterministic ranking using task-relevant terms
A random sample of files chosen each run
A very long summary of every file in the repo
questions.explanation: Task terms help select a small, relevant first read set.

questions.question: Which file should usually be read first when present?
options: A generated build bundle
The repository's root router
The largest binary file
An older, unrelated log entry
questions.explanation: The router explains how to navigate the workspace.

questions.question: What is the index not meant to replace?
options: The original task description text
Opening the authoritative source files
A single bare relative path string
A specific test command to run first here
questions.explanation: The index is a navigation aid, not a substitute for source inspection.
